claims.text: backend-review-checklist.md is used from stage-4 to review a backend design change (a pull request with an ADR or design document, or one touching a boundary, data or a limit); each question points at the document or ADR holding the expected answer; questions with an automated check point at it.

The checklist has six groups: data ownership and consistency; schema and message changes; security; resilience; SLOs and capacity; isolation between shops; then a worked example on reading the product list from db-replica.

Usage: go only through the groups a change touches; a small change in one module may need only one group, a change to a trust boundary or a load limit needs several; 'don't know' is a result, written as an open question in the pull request.

First group: new copy of data, two writers -> data-ownership.md; choice when the source is unreachable -> consistency-per-operation.md; another module's internal types -> ModuleBoundaryTests, DependencyRuleTests; service using another's database -> data-ownership.md, 'no check sees this'.

Checks: compiler plus ModuleBoundaryTests/DependencyRuleTests (module boundaries); Program.cs, RateLimitTests (new endpoint's limit); OrderMessageContractTests (message shape); CI build failing when a package it uses has a known vulnerability, and Grype per image (known vulnerabilities).

Rows pointing at decisions: ADR 0013 (shop_id, filter by shop from the access token), slo.md (requests counted good/bad), threat-model.md (trust boundaries), audit-log.md (actions to audit), multi-shop-data-rollout.md (CONCURRENTLY, lock_timeout), ADR 0016 (busy shop).
Worked example proposal: add a connection string to the replica and move GET /api/v1/products onto it to reduce load on the primary.

Worked example, consistency: consistency-per-operation.md allows the product list slightly old data and the list writes nothing back from what it reads, so it passes; ProductCache reads (also when ordering) stay on the primary: refilling it from a replica could put an old price back for a whole TTL.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/backend-review-checklist.md lines 76-79; docs/design/consistency-per-operation.md section 'Nếu chuyển đọc sang replica' @ stage-4

claims.text: Worked example, capacity: capacity-plan.md's trigger is peak product reads exceeding the primary's headroom; the PR must show the trigger has come or record why it moves early; the new connection string is one more connection pool in each api Pod, so the total is rechecked against max_connections.
PostgreSQL's max_connections is the server's limit on concurrent connections.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: Server Configuration > Connections and Authentication > max_connections

claims.text: Worked example, SLO: S3 in slo.md counts product GET requests not returning 5xx and is measured at the API, so replica errors appear in S3; a fallback to the primary is needed when the replica lags too far or does not answer, otherwise a broken replica spends S3's budget.

The example's four points fall in two groups (data ownership and consistency; SLOs and capacity). Data ownership: the replica is a new copy added to data-ownership.md, trust the primary. Conclusion: accept when the trigger has come, a fallback exists, data-ownership.md changes in the same PR.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/backend-review-checklist.md headings lines 18, 55; bullets lines 76-92 @ stage-4

claims.text: slo.md lists under 'Chưa có' that production has no Prometheus, so production's SLOs cannot be measured yet.
ADR 0016 (per-shop limits) is accepted but not built at stage-4; it waits for release 2 of multi-shop-data-rollout.md, which brings the shop from the access token.
OrderMessageContractTests fails a pull request that renames or retypes a message property on either side; fitness-functions.md maps each quality attribute to its check and records gaps.

claims.text: Opinion: when a change differs from the decision a row points at, either redesign the change or update the decision in the same pull request so it is reviewed too (generalised from the worked example's data-ownership.md edit and consistency-per-operation.md's 'update the table first').
claims.source_hint: docs/design/backend-review-checklist.md lines 87-92; docs/design/consistency-per-operation.md last line @ stage-4

claims.text: Opinion (trade-offs): reviewing design changes against touched groups and recorded decisions costs less than every question on every PR, which tends to skimming, and is steadier than reviewer judgment alone; checks alone miss what no check sees.

Opinion (choices): a private rename inside Ordering is not a design change, so ordinary code review applies; if a check for cross-service database use is added, the row points at it; an unanswerable budget question becomes an open question in the PR.

Opinion (misconceptions): the checklist does not replace knowledge of the system; no question names ProductCache, yet the worked example's ProductCache exclusion depends on knowing how prices are read; rows go stale when the documents, ADRs or checks they point at change.

Try it answers: index on a large table -> schema group row pointing at multi-shop-data-rollout.md (no check); optional message property -> OrderMessageContractTests; shop staff listing orders -> ADR 0013 (isolation), audit-log.md (security), Program.cs/RateLimitTests (resilience).
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY builds an index without locking out writes to the table; lock_timeout makes a statement give up when it waits longer than the set time for a lock.
